original_question: As in 17.57, let r(m) = {r + km | k ∈ Z} for integers 0 ⩽ r < m; for r1(m1) ∩ r2(m2) = ∅ let the class transposition τr1(m1),r2(m2) be the involution which interchanges r1 + tm1 and r2 + tm2 for each integer t and fixes everything else, and let CT(Z) be the group generated by all class transpositions. Let CTk be the subgroup of CT(Z) generated by the class transpositions τr1(k),r2(k) for 0 ⩽ r1 ̸= r2 < k. Since τr1(k),r2(k) permutes the residue classes modulo k, the group CTk is isomorphic to the symmetric group Sk. Let CT(k) = ⟨CT2, CT3,..., CTk ⟩. Is it true that for k > 3 the group CT(k) is isomorphic to the symmetric group SN, where N is the least common multiple of the numbers 2, 3,..., k?
self_contained_problem:
For integers $0 \le r < m$, let $r(m) = \{r + km \mid k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ denote the residue class $r$ modulo $m$. Given two disjoint residue classes $r_1(m_1)$ and $r_2(m_2)$ (i.e. $r_1(m_1) \cap r_2(m_2) = \emptyset$), define the class transposition $\tau_{r_1(m_1),\,r_2(m_2)} : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ to be the involution that interchanges $r_1 + t m_1$ with $r_2 + t m_2$ for each $t \in \mathbb{Z}$ and fixes every other integer. Let $\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ be the subgroup of the symmetric group on $\mathbb{Z}$ generated by all such class transpositions.

For an integer $k \ge 2$, let
$$\mathrm{CT}_k = \langle \tau_{r_1(k),\,r_2(k)} \mid 0 \le r_1 \ne r_2 < k \rangle \le \mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z}).$$
Since each generator permutes the $k$ residue classes modulo $k$ and acts as the corresponding transposition on these classes, $\mathrm{CT}_k \cong S_k$. Define
$$\mathrm{CT}^{(k)} = \langle \mathrm{CT}_2,\, \mathrm{CT}_3,\, \ldots,\, \mathrm{CT}_k \rangle.$$

Prove or disprove: for every integer $k > 3$,
$$\mathrm{CT}^{(k)} \cong S_N, \qquad \text{where } N = \mathrm{lcm}(2, 3, \ldots, k).$$
status_search_result: A 2026 preprint by Junyao Pan ("A note on the horizontal class transposition group", arXiv:2604.12553) claims to resolve the Bardakov–Iskra conjecture, proving that for $n > 3$, $\mathrm{CT}^{(n)} \cong S_N$ with $N = \mathrm{lcm}(2,3,\ldots,n)$.

original_question: Among globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds, is the total volume V(M) minimized exactly at the Fuchsian locus?
self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g \geq 2$, and let $M$ be a globally hyperbolic maximal Cauchy-compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter 3-manifold homeomorphic to $S \times \mathbb{R}$. Such manifolds form a deformation space parameterized (by the Mess theorem) by pairs of points in the Teichmüller space $\mathcal{T}(S) \times \mathcal{T}(S)$; the diagonal $\{(X,X) : X \in \mathcal{T}(S)\}$ is called the Fuchsian locus, and consists of those $M$ that contain a totally geodesic spacelike Cauchy surface. Let $V(M)$ denote the total Lorentzian volume of $M$ (which is finite for GHMC AdS 3-manifolds). 

Prove or disprove: among all GHMC anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds $M$ with underlying surface $S$, the volume $V(M)$ attains its minimum precisely on the Fuchsian locus, and this minimum value equals $\pi^2 |\chi(S)|$.
status_search_result: A 2026 preprint by Mondello and Tholozan ("Minimizing the volume of globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds", arXiv:2602.14806) proves that the volume of a GHMC anti-de Sitter 3-manifold $M$ is at least $\pi^2 |\chi(M)|$, with equality if and only if $M$ is Fuchsian, settling the question affirmatively.

paper_title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry
original_question: Is the total volume V(M) of a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold minimized at the Fuchsian locus?
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a closed orientable surface of genus g ≥ 2. A globally hyperbolic maximal compact (GHMC) anti-de Sitter 3-manifold is a Lorentzian 3-manifold M of constant sectional curvature −1, diffeomorphic to S × ℝ, that contains a closed spacelike Cauchy surface and is maximal (with respect to inclusion) among such manifolds. By a theorem of Mess, the moduli space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on S × ℝ is parametrized by Teich(S) × Teich(S), where Teich(S) is the Teichmüller space of S; the diagonal {(X,X) : X ∈ Teich(S)} is called the Fuchsian locus, consisting of those manifolds whose holonomy preserves a totally geodesic spacelike plane.

Each GHMC anti-de Sitter manifold M has a finite total volume V(M) (defined, e.g., as the volume of its convex core or, equivalently up to convention, the volume bounded by appropriate Cauchy surfaces in a canonical way).

Question: Is V(M) minimized over the moduli space of GHMC anti-de Sitter structures on S × ℝ precisely at (and only at) the Fuchsian locus?
status_search_result: A 2026 preprint by Mondello and Tholozan, "Minimizing the volume of globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds" (arXiv:2602.14806), proves that the volume of a maximal globally hyperbolic Cauchy-compact anti-de Sitter 3-manifold is at least π²|χ(S)|, with equality if and only if the manifold is Fuchsian, thus answering the question affirmatively. Earlier partial results (e.g., Bonsante–Seppi, GAFA 2017) had established related bounds and local rigidity near the Fuchsian locus.

original_question: Conjecture: Suppose that for a fixed positive integer k at least half of the elements of a finite group G have order k. Then G is solvable.
self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $k$ be a fixed positive integer. Suppose that the number of elements of $G$ of order exactly $k$ is at least $|G|/2$. Prove or disprove: $G$ must be solvable.
status_search_result: Recent work shows the conjecture as stated is false in general: counterexamples exist, and for every k>1 one can find finite non-solvable groups in which a positive proportion (at least 2/15) of elements have order k. The conjecture does hold in special cases (e.g., k a prime power, or k ∈ {2,3,4}), with classical results of Liebeck–MacHale covering the involution case.

original_question: Let (X, X, µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ). If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function with values in the closed unit disk that has convergent means, do the weighted averages (1/N) Σ Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge pointwise almost everywhere?
self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu,T)$ be a measure-preserving system, where $T:X\to X$ is an invertible measure-preserving transformation on a probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$. Let $f,g\in L^\infty(\mu)$.

Let $\Lambda$ denote the von Mangoldt function, defined by $\Lambda(n)=\log p$ if $n=p^k$ for some prime $p$ and integer $k\ge 1$, and $\Lambda(n)=0$ otherwise.

Let $\varphi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a multiplicative function (i.e. $\varphi(mn)=\varphi(m)\varphi(n)$ whenever $\gcd(m,n)=1$) with $|\varphi(n)|\le 1$ for all $n$, and assume that $\varphi$ has convergent mean, i.e. the limit
$$\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)$$
exists in $\mathbb{C}$.

Prove or disprove: for $\mu$-almost every $x\in X$, both of the weighted bilinear ergodic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\Lambda(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)\qquad\text{and}\qquad \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\varphi(n)\,f(T^n x)\,g(T^{2n} x)$$
converge as $N\to\infty$.
status_search_result: Recent work has resolved this problem. A 2026 preprint on bilinear ergodic averages with arithmetic weights explicitly states it resolves Problem 12 of Frantzikinakis' survey, proving almost sure convergence of $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n\le N} w(n) T^{an}f\cdot T^{bn}g$ for $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ where $w$ is the von Mangoldt function. A 2024 preprint also established pointwise a.e. convergence for Möbius-weighted (and more general multiplicative) bilinear averages with $P_1(n)=n$, $P_2(n)=2n$, again citing the resolution of Frantzikinakis' problem.

context_brief: Picard group of polarized K3 moduli
original_question: Let M_{2n}^{K3} be the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n. Do the Noether–Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group Pic(M_{2n}^{K3}) ⊗_Z Q?
self_contained_problem: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n}$ denote the moduli space of complex polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2n$, i.e., pairs $(X,L)$ where $X$ is a smooth complex K3 surface and $L$ is a primitive ample line bundle on $X$ with $L\cdot L = 2n$. For each pair of integers $(h,d)$ with $h\geq 1$ and $d>0$ satisfying suitable admissibility conditions, the Noether–Lefschetz locus $D_{h,d}\subset \mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n}$ parameterizes those polarized K3 surfaces $(X,L)$ whose Picard lattice has rank at least $2$ and contains a class $\beta$ with $\beta\cdot\beta = 2h-2$ and $\beta\cdot L = d$; each such locus is a divisor (a Noether–Lefschetz divisor) on $\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n}$. Question: Do the classes of the Noether–Lefschetz divisors $D_{h,d}$ span the rational Picard group $\mathrm{Pic}(\mathcal{M}^{K3}_{2n})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}}\mathbb{Q}$?
status_search_result: The Maulik–Pandharipande conjecture that Noether–Lefschetz divisors span the rational Picard group of the moduli space of polarized K3 surfaces of degree 2n was proved by Bergeron–Li–Millson–Moeglin ("The Noether–Lefschetz conjecture and generalizations", Invent. Math. 2017). Generalizations to orthogonal modular varieties (Heegner divisors generating the rational Picard group) have since been established by Bruinier–Möller and Bruinier–Zuffetti, and explicit finite generation results have appeared more recently.

paper_title: Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
original_question: For any fixed pair of quantum channels Φ and Ω, does there exist a number p* > 0 such that additivity of minimal output Rényi entropy, S^p_min(Φ ⊗ Ω) = S^p_min(Φ) + S^p_min(Ω), holds either for every p in an interval (p*,1) with p* < 1 or for every p in an interval (1,p*) with p* > 1?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_A)$ and $\Omega:\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)\to\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{K}_B)$ be quantum channels (completely positive trace-preserving linear maps between matrix algebras). For $p>0$, $p\neq 1$, the Rényi entropy of order $p$ of a density operator $\rho$ is
$$S^p(\rho)=\frac{1}{1-p}\log\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^p),$$
and for $p=1$ it is the von Neumann entropy $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{Tr}(\rho\log\rho)$. The minimal output Rényi $p$-entropy of a channel $\Phi$ is
$$S^p_{\min}(\Phi)=\inf_{\rho}S^p(\Phi(\rho)),$$
where the infimum is over input density operators (equivalently, pure states).

Decide the following statement: for every pair of quantum channels $\Phi$ and $\Omega$, there exists $p^*>0$ such that either
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $p^*<1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(p^*,1)$, or
\item[(ii)] $p^*>1$ and $S^p_{\min}(\Phi\otimes\Omega)=S^p_{\min}(\Phi)+S^p_{\min}(\Omega)$ holds for every $p\in(1,p^*)$.
\end{enumerate}
That is, prove this dichotomy holds for all channel pairs, or exhibit a counterexample.
category_tag: Quantum channels and Rényi entropy additivity
status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be refuted. Hastings (2009) produced channels for which additivity of minimum output von Neumann entropy fails at $p=1$; subsequent analyses (Aubrun–Szarek–Werner; Cubitt–Harrow–Leung–Montanaro–Winter; Collins–Fukuda–Nechita and others) show that the same random-subspace constructions yield violations of additivity of the minimum output Rényi $p$-entropy on intervals adjacent to $p=1$ (in particular for $p\in(1-p_0,1)$ with $p_0\approx 0.2855$). Combined with Hayden–Winter / Grudka–Horodecki / recent constructive results showing violations for all $p>1$, there exist fixed pairs $(\Phi,\Omega)$ for which additivity fails on every one-sided neighborhood of $p=1$, contradicting the conjectured dichotomy.

paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
original_question: Let Ω be the unit ball in R^3 and let λ1 = π^2 be the first eigenvalue of -Δ on Ω with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. For 0 < λ ≤ λ1/4, does the boundary value problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit a smooth nontrivial solution u not identically zero?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^3 : |x| < 1\}$ be the open unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$, and let $\lambda_1 = \pi^2$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$. Consider the semilinear elliptic boundary value problem with the critical Sobolev exponent
$$-\Delta u = u^5 + \lambda u \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial \Omega,$$
where $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$ is a parameter and the unknown $u : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function.

Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda$ with $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$, the problem admits a smooth solution $u \not\equiv 0$.
status_search_result: A 2025 preprint by Chen, Wei and others titled "On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution" (arXiv:2503.06904) claims a complete resolution of this problem, constructing infinitely many sign-changing, non-radial smooth solutions for the full parameter range, including $0 < \lambda \le \lambda_1/4$. The result has been announced but as of May 2026 is still in preprint/peer-review status.

original_question: For integers q >= p >= 3, what is the maximum spectral radius among graphs in G(m, theta_{1,p,q})? Equivalently, characterize the extremal graphs with m edges that avoid the theta graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths 1, p, and q between the same two endpoints.
self_contained_problem:
For integers $q \ge p \ge 3$, the theta graph $\theta_{1,p,q}$ is the graph obtained from two distinct vertices $u,v$ by joining them with three internally disjoint paths of lengths $1$, $p$, and $q$ (so $\theta_{1,p,q}$ has the edge $uv$ together with two internally disjoint $u$-$v$ paths of lengths $p$ and $q$). For a positive integer $m$, let $\mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$ denote the family of simple graphs with exactly $m$ edges that contain no subgraph isomorphic to $\theta_{1,p,q}$. The spectral radius $\rho(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix.

Determine, for all integers $q \ge p \ge 3$ and all sufficiently large $m$, the maximum value of $\rho(G)$ over $G \in \mathcal{G}(m, \theta_{1,p,q})$, and characterize all graphs attaining this maximum.
status_search_result: The problem, posed by Li, Zhao and Zou (2025) as Problem 8 concerning the maximum spectral radius among $\theta_{1,p,q}$-free graphs with $m$ edges, has reportedly been resolved completely; a recent survey/paper indicates that two of its theorems (corresponding to Theorem 3.27 and Theorem 3.36) together solve this problem. Independent confirmation via search was limited, so the resolution rests on this single source.

paper_title: Open Problems, Questions, and Challenges in Finite-Dimensional Integrable Systems
original_question: Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliat ed by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed plane curve (with positive curvature) bounding a convex domain $K$. The outer billiard map $T$ about $\gamma$ is defined on $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K$ as follows: for a point $p$ outside $K$, let $\ell$ be the right tangent line from $p$ to $\gamma$, touching $\gamma$ at the point $q$; then $T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ through $q$, i.e. $T(p)=2q-p$.

Suppose that there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $\gamma$ in $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K$ (or, more strongly, the entire exterior $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K$) that is foliated by continuous closed curves each of which is invariant under $T$. Prove that $\gamma$ must be an ellipse.
status_search_result: A 2024 result by M. Bialy ("Integrable outer billiards and rigidity", Journal of Modern Dynamics) establishes that if the exterior of a smooth strictly convex curve of positive curvature is foliated by continuous curves invariant under the outer billiard map, then the curve must be an ellipse. The proof introduces a new generating function and uses an integral-geometric argument reducing to the Blaschke–Santaló inequality. This resolves the smooth (total) version of the outer Birkhoff conjecture as stated.

paper_title: Open problems about regular languages, 35 years later.
original_question: For a finite semigroup S, define its group complexity to be the smallest integer n such that S divides a wreath product A0 ∘ G1 ∘ A1 ∘ ⋯ ∘ A_{n-1} ∘ Gn ∘ An, where the Ai are aperiodic semigroups and the Gi are groups. Given the multiplication table of a finite semigroup, is there an algorithm that computes its group complexity?
self_contained_problem:
Let S be a finite semigroup. By the Krohn–Rhodes theorem, every finite semigroup divides a wreath product of the form

  A_0 ∘ G_1 ∘ A_1 ∘ ⋯ ∘ A_{n-1} ∘ G_n ∘ A_n,

where A_0, A_1, …, A_n are finite aperiodic semigroups (semigroups whose subgroups are all trivial) and G_1, …, G_n are finite groups. Here "divides" means S is a homomorphic image of a subsemigroup, and ∘ denotes the wreath product of (transformation) semigroups. Define the group complexity (Krohn–Rhodes complexity) c(S) of S to be the smallest nonnegative integer n for which such a decomposition of S exists.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input the multiplication table of an arbitrary finite semigroup S, computes the group complexity c(S)?
status_search_result: A 2024 preprint by Margolis, Rhodes, and Schilling ("Decidability of Krohn-Rhodes complexity for all finite semigroups and automata", arXiv:2406.18477) announces a proof that Krohn–Rhodes (group) complexity is decidable for every nonnegative integer k, building on earlier work establishing decidability of complexity c = 1 (arXiv:2110.10373) and a reduction showing decidability of c = 1 implies decidability for all n ≥ 0. The problem, open for over 50 years, thus appears to be resolved, although the proof is recent and verification by the community is ongoing.

original_question: Assume that the exterior of an outer billiard table is foliated by invariant curves. Prove that the table is an ellipse.
self_contained_problem:
Let $\gamma \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex closed plane curve (of positive curvature), bounding a convex region $K$. The outer (dual) billiard map $T$ is defined on the exterior $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ as follows: for a point $p$ outside $K$, consider the right tangent line from $p$ to $\gamma$ (using a fixed orientation), and let $q$ be the point of tangency; then $T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ in $q$, i.e., $q$ is the midpoint of the segment $[p, T(p)]$.

Suppose the exterior $\mathbb{R}^2 \setminus K$ is foliated by a continuous family of closed curves each of which is invariant under $T$ (i.e., the outer billiard around $\gamma$ is totally integrable in this sense).

Prove that $\gamma$ must be an ellipse.
status_search_result: A 2024 result by M. Bialy in the Journal of Modern Dynamics ("Integrable outer billiards and rigidity") proves precisely that if the exterior of a smooth strictly convex plane curve of positive curvature is foliated by continuous curves invariant under the outer billiard map, then the curve must be an ellipse. The proof introduces a new generating function for outer billiards and integral-geometric weights reducing the problem to the Blaschke–Santaló inequality.

original_question: At t = 0, do the symplectic and orthogonal squared-content generating functions both reduce to ∏_{j≥1} 1/(1 - x^{4j-2}) as stated in Conjecture 6.3(b)?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer partition $\lambda$ of $n$ (written $\lambda \vdash n$), regard $\lambda$ as a Young diagram and, for each cell $u=(i,j)\in\lambda$ (with $i$ the row index and $j$ the column index, both starting at $1$), define:

- the hook length $h(u) = \lambda_i - j + \lambda'_j - i + 1$, where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content $c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j + 2 & \text{if } i \le j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j - 2 & \text{if } i > j; \end{cases}$
- the orthogonal content $c_{O}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j & \text{if } i < j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j & \text{if } i \ge j. \end{cases}$

Prove or disprove that, as formal power series in $x$,
$$\sum_{n\ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u)^2}{h(u)^2} \;=\; \sum_{n\ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{O}(u)^2}{h(u)^2} \;=\; \prod_{j\ge 1} \frac{1}{1 - x^{4j-2}}.$$

original_question: Do the symplectic and orthogonal squared-content sums both satisfy the content Nekrasov-Okounkov formula in Conjecture 6.3(a): Σ_{n≥0} x^n Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_sp(u)^2)/h(u)^2 = Σ_{n≥0} x^n Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_O(u)^2)/h(u)^2 = (∏_{j≥1} 1/(1 - x^{4j-2})) (∏_{j≥1} 1/(1-x^j)^t)?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer partition λ = (λ₁ ≥ λ₂ ≥ ⋯) of n, identified with its Young diagram, and for a cell u = (i,j) in λ (with i the row index and j the column index, both starting at 1), define:
- the hook length h(u) = λᵢ − j + λ′ⱼ − i + 1, where λ′ is the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content c_sp(u) = j + λ′ⱼ − i if i ≤ j, and c_sp(u) = i + λᵢ − j − 1 if i > j;
- the orthogonal content c_O(u) = j + λ′ⱼ − i − 1 if i ≤ j, and c_O(u) = i + λᵢ − j if i > j.

∑_{n≥0} xⁿ ∑_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_sp(u)²)/h(u)²
 = ∑_{n≥0} xⁿ ∑_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_O(u)²)/h(u)²

original_question: At the specialization t = 0, are the symplectic and orthogonal content generating functions equal, and do they both reduce to ∏_{j≥1} 1/(1 + x^{4j-2}) as claimed in Conjecture 6.2(c)?
self_contained_problem:
Let $\lambda \vdash n$ denote a partition of $n$, drawn as a Young diagram with cells $u = (i,j)$ (row $i$, column $j$, $1$-indexed). For a cell $u = (i,j) \in \lambda$ define:
- the hook length $h(u) = \lambda_i - j + \lambda'_j - i + 1$, where $\lambda'$ is the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content
$$c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j + 2, & i < j, \\ \lambda_i + \lambda_i - 2i + 2, & i = j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j - 2, & i > j; \end{cases}$$
- the orthogonal content
$$c_{\mathrm{O}}(u) = \begin{cases} \lambda_i + \lambda_j - i - j, & i \le j, \\ -\lambda'_i - \lambda'_j + i + j, & i > j. \end{cases}$$
(Here $\lambda_i$ is set to $0$ for $i$ exceeding the length of $\lambda$, and similarly for $\lambda'$.)

Prove or disprove the following identity of formal power series in $x$:
$$\sum_{n \ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{\mathrm{sp}}(u)}{h(u)} \;=\; \sum_{n \ge 0} x^n \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{c_{\mathrm{O}}(u)}{h(u)} \;=\; \prod_{j \ge 1} \frac{1}{1 + x^{4j-2}}.$$

original_question: For symplectic contents c_sp(u), is the generating function Σ_{n≥0} x^n Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (t + c_sp(u))/h(u) equal to the infinite product stated in Conjecture 6.2(a)?
self_contained_problem:
For an integer partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots)$ of $n$, identify $\lambda$ with its Young diagram, and for a cell $u=(i,j)\in\lambda$ define:
- the hook length $h(u)=\lambda_i-j+\lambda'_j-i+1$, where $\lambda'$ denotes the conjugate partition;
- the symplectic content
$$c_{sp}(u)=\begin{cases} j-i, & \text{if } j>i,\\ i+j-1, & \text{if } j\le i.\end{cases}$$

Let $t$ be a formal parameter and $q$ a formal variable. Prove or disprove that
$$\sum_{n\ge 0} q^{n}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\prod_{u\in\lambda}\frac{t+c_{sp}(u)}{h(u)}=\prod_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(1-q^{8n})^{\binom{t+1}{2}}}{(1-q^{8n-2})^{\binom{t+1}{2}-1}}\cdot\left(\frac{1-q^{4n-1}}{1-q^{4n-3}}\right)^{t}\cdot\left(\frac{1-q^{8n-4}}{1-q^{8n-6}}\right)^{\binom{t}{2}-1},$$
as an identity of formal power series in $q$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}[t]$.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every isotropic logconcave density f on R^n satisfies f(0) ≤ C^n? In the equivalent convex-body form highlighted in the paper, does every isotropic convex body in R^n have volume at least c^n for some absolute constant c?
self_contained_problem:
A probability density $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to[0,\infty)$ is called log-concave if $\log f$ is concave on its support (with the convention $\log 0=-\infty$). Such a density is called isotropic if its barycenter is the origin, i.e. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x\, f(x)\,dx = 0$, and its covariance matrix is the identity, i.e. $\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} x_i x_j f(x)\,dx = \delta_{ij}$ for all $1\le i,j\le n$.

Question: Does there exist an absolute constant $C>0$ (independent of $n$) such that for every dimension $n\ge 1$ and every isotropic log-concave probability density $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$,
$$f(0) \le C^n\,?$$

Equivalently (in the convex-body form): a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of unit volume with barycenter at the origin is called isotropic if there is a constant $L_K>0$ with $\int_K \langle x,\theta\rangle^2\, dx = L_K^2$ for every unit vector $\theta\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that every isotropic convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ (so with unit volume) satisfies, after suitable normalization, a uniform bound $L_K\le C$ for an absolute constant $C$ — equivalently, that the isotropic constant $L_K$ is bounded above by a universal constant independent of the dimension $n$?
status_search_result: Bourgain's slicing/hyperplane conjecture has been resolved. Building on a small-ball estimate of Qingyang Guan (2024), Bo'az Klartag and Joseph Lehec announced a proof in December 2024 (arXiv:2501.06854, "The slicing conjecture via small ball estimates") establishing that the isotropic constant of log-concave probability densities in R^n is bounded by an absolute constant independent of dimension, equivalently $f(0) \le C^n$ for isotropic log-concave $f$.

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: If X is drawn from an isotropic logconcave density f on R^n, must the variance of the squared Euclidean norm ||X||^2 always be at most Cn for some absolute constant C? Equivalently, must isotropic logconcave measures have most of their mass concentrated in a thin Euclidean shell of constant-width scale after normalization?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let f: R^n → [0,∞) be a log-concave probability density (i.e., f = e^{-V} for some convex V: R^n → (-∞,∞]) that is isotropic, meaning that if X is a random vector with density f then E[X] = 0 and the covariance matrix of X equals the n×n identity, E[X X^T] = I_n. Prove or disprove: there exists an absolute constant C > 0, independent of n and f, such that for every such X,

  Var(‖X‖_2^2) ≤ C n,

where ‖·‖_2 denotes the Euclidean norm on R^n. Equivalently, show that every isotropic log-concave probability measure on R^n concentrates most of its mass in a Euclidean shell of constant width about the sphere of radius √n.
status_search_result: Recent work by Klartag and Lehec (2024–2025), building on a parallel-coupling/stochastic-localization technique introduced by Guan in the resolution of Bourgain's slicing conjecture, established the thin-shell conjecture: for isotropic log-concave X in R^n one has Var(‖X‖^2) ≤ C n with an absolute constant C. The result is reported in expository accounts and the 2025 preprint "Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling" (arXiv:2507.15495).

paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every convex body K in R^n admits an ellipsoid E with the following approximate sandwiching property: at least half the volume of E lies inside K, and at least half the volume of K lies inside the dilated ellipsoid C log n · E?
self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let K ⊂ ℝⁿ be a convex body (a compact convex set with non-empty interior). For an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝⁿ centered at some point and a scalar t > 0, write tE for the dilation of E by factor t about its center. Determine whether the following holds:

There exists an absolute constant C > 0 (independent of n and K) such that for every n ≥ 2 and every convex body K ⊂ ℝⁿ, one can find an ellipsoid E ⊂ ℝⁿ satisfying simultaneously
  (i) vol(E ∩ K) ≥ (1/2) · vol(E),
  (ii) vol(K ∩ (C log n) · E) ≥ (1/2) · vol(K),
where vol denotes Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ.

Prove or disprove the existence of such a constant C.
status_search_result: The conjectured approximate ellipsoidal sandwiching with a C·log n factor follows from (and is now far surpassed by) the resolution of Bourgain's slicing/hyperplane conjecture by Klartag and Lehec (using a key bound of Guan), announced in December 2024, and the subsequent thin-shell bound of Klartag–Lehec (2025). For an isotropic convex body the inertia ellipsoid gives the sandwiching with an absolute constant (in particular better than C log n) once the thin-shell/isotropic-constant bounds are constants. Hence the stated conjecture is affirmatively resolved.

paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
original_question: Fix natural numbers a1,...,ar. Does there exist a number q, depending only on these degrees, such that for every polynomial ring W over k and every homogeneous ideal J with minimal homogeneous generator degrees a1,...,ar, the regularity reg(W/J) is at most q, independently of the number of variables of W?
self_contained_problem: Fix natural numbers $a_1,\dots,a_r$. Does there exist a number $q = q(a_1,\dots,a_r)$, depending only on the degrees $a_1,\dots,a_r$, such that the following holds: for every field $k$, every polynomial ring $W = k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ (with any number $n$ of variables) endowed with the standard grading, and every homogeneous ideal $J \subset W$ admitting a minimal homogeneous system of generators of degrees exactly $a_1,\dots,a_r$, the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity satisfies $\operatorname{reg}(W/J) \le q$, with the bound independent of $n$?
status_search_result: This is the regularity version of Stillman's conjecture. Stillman's conjecture (uniform bound on projective dimension depending only on the generator degrees) was proved by Ananyan and Hochster (2016/2020). Combined with a theorem of Caviglia bounding regularity in terms of projective dimension and generator degrees, this yields an affirmative answer: a uniform bound on reg(W/J) depending only on a_1,...,a_r exists, independent of the number of variables. Subsequent work by Erman–Sam–Snowden and Draisma–Lasoń–Leykin gave alternative proofs, and explicit bounds have been pursued in later work.
